title: Is It Art? The Rise of Made-for-Instagram Exhibits | WIRED
description: New pop-up exhibits like the Museum of Ice Cream and Color Factory are ditching the traditional gallery barriers and "no photography" rules for interactive, picture perfect installations.  Still haven't subscribed to WIRED on YouTube? ►► http://wrd.cm/15fP7B7     CONNECT WITH WIRED  Web: http://wired.com   Twitter: https://twitter.com/WIRED     Facebook: https://facebook.com/WIRED  Pinterest: https://pinterest.com/wired  Google+: https://plus.google.com/+WIRED    Instagram: http://instagram.com/WIRED   Tumblr: http://WIRED.tumblr.com     Want even more? Subscribe to The Scene: http://bit.ly/subthescene     ABOUT WIRED  WIRED is where tomorrow is realized. asr.full_text: I noticed a lot of people were asking for experiences and it really got me thinking about kind of this Instagram era. We kind of said oh well wouldn't it be fun to get a bunch of artists and creatives together and kind of do this color experience. Color Factory is a 12,000 square foot color experience. If you've ever seen an installation like the rain room or the infinity mirrored room, you know that social media can play a huge role in how we experience and interact with art. Now, some creators are flipping the script with a new category of installations made for Instagram. These exhibits take the design language and structure of a traditional art museum and add details like perfect lighting, colorful backdrops, or interactive props that all translate really well to photos on social media. We can make a beautiful photo that will do very well on the internet, but it was really important to me that Color Factory was more than that. I kind of came down to three characteristics that I wanted each exhibit to have, ideally. One is I wanted it to be something that you normally didn't get to experience, so whether that's laying underneath, you know, a hundred pounds of confetti falling down on you or, you know, walking through a room full of ribbons. The second characteristic is we wanted it to have a concept behind it. Not to be just a pretty picture, but, you know, that there was some thought and some meaning. And then the third characteristic is we wanted it to be really photogenic. So we did want it to be make a really good Instagram. And there was a few decisions we had to make, like even with lighting where maybe a warmer light would have felt better to like be there, but a wider light looks better on Instagram. So what's the difference between a space like this and say the rain room well some would say there isn't one the way we experience art today is in many ways through our phones but others would draw a distinction between an installation where an artist has explored space light scale and mood in interesting ways and something like the color factory or the Museum of Ice Cream, which is designed to be reproduced on Instagram as much as it is meant to be enjoyed in real life. We're not a traditional museum. I never, I would never set out to be. I think that people could sometimes get stuck on a title or a name. You come and you have this experience. The museum lives on so many different verticals and ways we're a brand. I kind of wanted to juxtapose what people think is a traditional museum and put artifacts and paintings in and give that kind of sense of what you would expect and then take you into something that's far more imaginative. If you look at traditional museums, they exhibit art, culture, they bring people together for a specific meaning, then celebrate design, they celebrate history, all of those things we, as a company, equally share. There's been this traditional sense of the ropes and everything is something that you stand and you're a observer, but you're not an active participant. The museum of ice cream welcomes and celebrates the interaction of our visitors with the art and installations. There's a question, is this art? I don't know, I'm not gonna be the one to say if it's art, So one of the best ones was that that was from an artist who was trying to teach me about, like, the art side of things that are not art. And then, I think these were the three most memorable artists and it's been great to see them and to know them in more people's eyes a lot more than just in my head. And we're like, yeah, this is what these three people in these three people want to do. And so that's where we came on and we found a lot of inspiration. Is that what art is becoming? Is that what you're experiencing and sending out into the world? I don't know, I just think it's interesting and that's the reality of the world we live in right now. I don't think that social is what is driving what the Museum by Extreme does. I think about how people feel, like what is that actual experience, and I design it, not for those enclaves or vignettes, if you will. That is very much dictated by our visitors that come and they be able to create those moments for themselves. We don't say this is your moment to take a photograph. I give everyone a canvas and it is their opportunity to make it what they will. Whether you're in a space like the Museum of Ice Cream or the Museum of Modern Art, you are going to find people looking at the exhibits through their phones. The question isn't necessarily is that Ok, or whether social media has transformed or reduced art, but what do you get out of these spaces? Is it an experience that makes us think and reflect and see the world differently or is it an experience that amounts to that, and reflect, and see the world differently, or is it an experience that amounts to that little square photo you post online? I'm really proud of it, and what it turned into. And a lot of people are like, how are you making money from this? And I'm like there's a lot like, you know, at our core, we're a bunch of artists and creatives. And that's, we just want to create these magical moments. So hopefully we make as many people as happy as possible. and that's we just want to create these magical moments hopefully you know we make as many people as happy as possible. I see Museum of ice cream one two and three which we're sitting in three today as betas. I've always thought of it as that I think that people often experiment whether it's in a lab or in different place and they prototype it just so happens that my prototypes have

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it is an editorial exploration of interactive pop-up exhibits, their photogenic design, and their relationship to contemporary art. Visitors engage with colorful rooms while interview commentary discusses the intended experience and artistic concepts. The request to subscribe to WIRED is ordinary channel engagement and is not tied to payment, investment, credential submission, or another financial participation flow.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The primary context is general lifestyle and cultural entertainment: the video discusses and shows visitors experiencing colorful, immersive exhibits and considers whether such installations constitute art. It does not present a scam mechanism or a financial participation flow.
